h: A Ring With a Proper Pedigree
p: Part of what makes this show special is its history. The circus has been part of the Tower since it opened in the 1890s, and it sits between the four legs of the Tower itself, which is a fact that never stops being impressive once you know it. Generations of families have sat in these seats, and plenty of grandparents still talk fondly about Charlie Cairoli, the legendary clown who entertained Tower audiences for decades in the middle of the last century.

The setting is intimate compared with a modern arena, so even the cheaper seats feel close to the action. Kids who sit near the ring may find themselves in the line of fire for a bit of clowning, so if you've got a shy one, a seat a few rows back might suit them better.

A few tips for the day: arrive in good time so you're not squeezing past knees once the show has started, and sort toilet trips and snacks before you take your seats. Little ones can get restless during longer shows, so a short run on the beach beforehand can work wonders.

Afterwards, you're bang on the Promenade, so it's an easy hop to North Pier or Central Pier, a stroll on the sand, or a tram ride along the front. If you've still got legs left, the Tower Top's views are the perfect way to round things off.
